messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "The air’s changed — people are talking openly now, even at work. My friend at the ministry just said the office feels “boring,” which in our language means the fear is gone. We should keep quiet, but stay ready."
Sender 2: "The air’s changed — people are talking more freely, even joking, like they’ve stopped fearing the walls. I’ve been quietly gathering supplies and making sure everyone’s covered; if things shift, we need to be ready, but not loud about it."
Sender 3: "The markets are quiet today, but the talk’s louder than ever—people aren’t just complaining, they’re naming names. Something’s shifting, and it’s not just in the city."
Sender 4: "The pharmacy’s been quiet lately — I saw our pharmacist stocking up on meds again. Not for sale, just… hoarding. Feels like everyone’s holding their breath, waiting for something to snap. Let’s keep our heads down, but stay in touch — things are shifting faster than we thought."
Sender 5: "The weather’s getting cold early this year—better start thinking about extra blankets. I’ve been hearing the same quiet warnings from a few trusted folks lately; seems like everyone’s just waiting for the next move, but no one’s saying what it is."
Sender 6: "Just wanted to say — things feel different lately. Noticed the quiet ones around us are starting to talk, and even the usual signs are shifting. Maybe it’s nothing, but I’ve been telling people to keep their heads down and stay close to home this month."
Sender 7: "Hey — just got word from the usual channel: the city’s running quieter than usual, but in a way that feels… loose. The shops are open late, people are talking freely, even the old grocer said something about “not holding our breath.” Be careful what you say, but don’t overthink it — if it’s quiet now, it’s not because they’re in control. They’re just waiting."
Sender 8: "The quiet ones are starting to talk now — not out of hope, but because they’ve stopped believing the noise matters. We’re seeing the same signs everywhere, and if the silence stretches much longer, it won’t be fear keeping people still."
Sender 9: "Just got word from the usual channels — things feel different this week. The air’s tense but not in the usual way; like everyone’s holding their breath, waiting for the next move. Be careful what you say, and keep your lines quiet."
Sender 10: "The air feels different — like people are holding their breath but already moving forward. I’ve been keeping an eye on things, and while nothing’s broken yet, the quiet signs are adding up. Let’s stay sharp, keep communication light, and watch how the next few days play out."

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 10 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 10.
